text:
Dmitry Orlov is 35, a Stanley Cup winner with Washington in 2018, and these days a steadying veteran on a young Sharks team that is finally winning a few. On Saturday against Utah he had a goal and three assists, and he now has 14 points in 22 games, eight of them on the power play.

Our form check says to enjoy it without believing all of it. Nine points in his last ten is about double what his ice time usually produces, and the chances behind it are ordinary: mostly bounces, so expect it to cool. His three goals came on less than one expected goal. San Jose takes only 42% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at five on five with him on the ice, a little worse than without him, and his minutes are down more than two a night over the last ten games.

Evolving-Hockey had him just above replacement last season, with nearly all his value from the power play. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking still likes his gap at the blue line (15% of entries stopped, against 11% typical). He's useful in a defined role, which is what this looks like.
